questions.q: Which direction did the temple face in Ezekiel’s vision?
What did Ezekiel see at the gate facing east?
questions.a: Ezekiel saw water flowing from the gate facing east, on its south side.

questions.q: How deep did the water become that Ezekiel saw?
questions.a: The water became a river that was too deep to pass without swimming.

questions.q: What were on both sides of the river?
questions.a: On both sides of the river, the riverbank had many trees.

questions.q: To where did this water flow, and what did it do there?
questions.a: This water flowed to the Salt Sea and would restore it to freshness.

questions.q: What would not be made fresh at the Salt Sea?
questions.a: The swamps and marshes would not be made fresh at the Salt Sea.

questions.q: What kind of trees would grow on the riverbanks, and how would they grow?
questions.a: Edible trees would grow on the riverbanks, bearing fruit each month and never withering.

questions.q: Who would receive two portions of land among the tribes of Israel?
questions.a: Joseph would receive two portions of land among the tribes of Israel.

questions.q: The northern boundary of the land would reach to the border of what city?
questions.a: The northern boundary of the land would reach to the border of Damascus.

questions.q: What would be the eastern border of the land?
questions.a: The eastern border of the land would be the Jordan River.

questions.q: What brook would be part of the southern border of the land?
questions.a: The Brook of Egypt would be part of the southern border of the land.

questions.q: What would be the western border of the land?
questions.a: The western border of the land would be the Great Sea.

questions.q: How were the Israelites to determine the inheritances for each person in the land?
questions.a: The Israelites were to throw lots to determine the inheritance for each person in the land.

questions.q: Who were to be treated just like the native born people of Israel?
questions.a: Foreigners living in the midst of the Israelites were to be treated just like the native born people of Israel.

commentary.text: These waters signify the gospel of Christ, which went forth from Jerusalem, and spread into the countries about; also the gifts and powers of the Holy Ghost which accompanied it, by virtue of which is spread far, and produced blessed effects. Christ is the Temple; and he is the Door; from him the living waters flow, out of his pierced side. They are increasing waters. Observe the progress of the gospel in the world, and the process of the work of grace in the heart; attend the motions of the blessed Spirit under Divine guidance. If we search into the things of God, we find some things plain and easy to be understood, as the waters that were but to the ankles; others more difficult, which require a deeper search, as the waters to the knees, or the loins; and some quite beyond our reach, which we cannot penetrate; but must, as St. Paul did, adore the depth, Rom. 11. It is wisdom to begin with that which is most easy, before we proceed to that which is dark and hard to be understood. The promises of the sacred word, and the privileges of believers, as shed abroad in their souls by the quickening Spirit, abound where the gospel is preached; they nourish and delight the souls of men; they never fade nor wither, nor are exhausted. Even the leaves serve as medicines to the soul: the warnings and reproofs of the word, though less pleasant than Divine consolations, tend to heal the diseases of the soul. All who believe in Christ, and are united to him by his sanctifying Spirit, will share the privileges of Israelites. There is room in the church, and in heaven, for all who seek the blessings of that new covenant of which Christ is Mediator.
